title: Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements
summary: Control (Ind AS 110) · consolidation procedure, NCI, intra-group, ownership changes, loss of control · joint arrangements (Ind AS 111) · equity method (Ind AS 28) · separate FS (Ind AS 27) · Ind AS 112
currency: SM May 2026 onwards (Nov 2024 ed., Aug 2025 reprint) · questions swept May 2022 – Nov 2026 RTP/MTP

cards.front: Who must consolidate, the exemption and exceptions: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A parent presents consolidated financial statements. Exemption (para 4(a)) — all of: (i) it is a wholly or partly owned subsidiary and all owners are informed and do not object; (ii) its debt or equity is not traded in a public market; (iii) it has not filed, and is not filing, financial statements with a regulator to issue instruments in a public market; (iv) its ultimate or intermediate parent produces Ind AS consolidated statements available for public use. Exceptions : post-employment and long-term employee benefit plans (Ind AS 19) are not consolidated; an investment entity measuring all subsidiaries at FVTPL need not consolidate.
back.explanation: Indian GAAP exclusions for temporary control and severe long-term restrictions do not exist under Ind AS 110. Gratuity trust: accounted under Ind AS 19, not consolidated (SM Example 1).
cases: Gratuity trust: accounted under Ind AS 19, not consolidated (SM Example 1).

cards.front: Memory hook: Scope, exemption from consolidation?

back.simplified: Exempt only if all four: owners don't object, not listed, not filing, parent publishes Ind AS consolidated FS.

cards.front: Control: the three elements: what is the rule?

back.simplified: An investor controls an investee if and only if it has all three: (a) power over the investee; (b) exposure, or rights, to variable returns from its involvement; and (c) the ability to use its power to affect the amount of its returns . Reassess when facts indicate a change in any element. Only one investor can control an investee; if control is shared or absent, apply Ind AS 111, 28 or 109.
back.explanation: Control under Ind AS 110 is principle-based; AS 21 used quantitative tests (more than half the votes or control of the board) and could give two parents. Five parties each 20% with decisions needing any four of five → power shared, no one controls, not joint control either (SM Example 2).
cases: Five parties each 20% with decisions needing any four of five → power shared, no one controls, not joint control either (SM Example 2).

cards.front: Memory hook: Control = power + returns + link?

back.simplified: Control = P-R-L: Power, Returns, Link.

cards.front: Power: existing rights, current ability, relevant activities: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Power = existing rights that give the current ability to direct the relevant activities (activities that significantly affect the investee's returns — selling and buying, managing financial assets, acquiring/disposing assets, R&D, funding, budgets, appointing key management). When different investors direct different relevant activities, the one directing the activities that most significantly affect returns has power. Current ability exists even if not exercised, and where decisions arise only on particular events.
back.explanation: Rights giving power: voting/potential voting rights; rights to appoint or remove key management or the entity that directs; rights to direct or veto transactions; management contracts. SM Illustrations 3–5 (different investors directing different activities).
cases: SM Illustrations 3–5 (different investors directing different activities).

cards.front: Substantive vs protective rights: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Only substantive rights count: the holder must have the practical ability to exercise them (no barriers such as penalties, high exercise price, narrow timing, no mechanism, no information, operational or legal barriers; a mechanism for collective exercise; the holder benefits from exercise). Usually currently exercisable, but a right exercisable before decisions must be taken can be substantive (option to go from 30% to 70% exercisable in 25 days when the meeting is in 30 days). Protective rights protect the holder's interest without giving power — fundamental changes or exceptional circumstances (lender's rights on default, minority approval of extraordinary capex or new issues, approval of
back.explanation: Investor substantive + others protective → investor has power; investor protective + others substantive → others have power; both substantive → evaluate further. A lender's nominee director is protective only if it does not give board majority.
cases: SM Illustrations 6–9.

cards.front: Memory hook: Substantive vs protective rights?

back.simplified: Substantive = can and would exercise in time. Protective = only guards, never directs.

cards.front: Power through voting rights, de facto control and potential voting rights: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A majority of voting rights gives power where relevant activities are directed by majority vote or a majority appoints the governing body (unless rights are not substantive or another party has the right to direct). Power without a majority : contractual arrangement with other vote holders; rights from other contracts; the investor's own holding being sufficient ( de facto control — size relative to the size and dispersion of other holdings, number of parties needed to outvote); potential voting rights if substantive; or a combination. If still unclear, consider voting patterns at previous meetings; if still unclear, no control.
back.explanation: Economic dependence alone (supplier on its main customer) does not give power. SM Illustrations 10–13 (45% with widely dispersed holders; voting patterns).
cases: SM Illustrations 10–13 (45% with widely dispersed holders; voting patterns).

cards.front: Variable returns, principal vs agent, de facto agents: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Variable returns can be positive, negative or both, judged on substance (fixed bond interest and fixed fees are variable for this purpose because of credit/performance risk). A decision maker that is an agent does not control. Factors: scope of decision-making authority; rights held by others (a single party able to remove without cause → agent); remuneration (commensurate and at arm's length suggests agent); exposure from other interests (greater variability → principal). Treat rights of de facto agents (related parties, parties funded by or restricted by the investor, common boards, close business relations) as the investor's own.
back.explanation: Investor 30% + fellow subsidiary 30% it can direct → 60% → control; with only 10% more → no control (SM Example 5). Reputational risk alone is not a basis for consolidation.
cases: Investor 30% + fellow subsidiary 30% it can direct → 60% → control; with only 10% more → no control (SM Example 5).
SM Illustrations 17–20 (fund managers).

cards.front: Silos and continuous assessment: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A portion of an investee is a deemed separate entity (silo) if specified assets are the only source of payment for specified liabilities or interests, and no other party has rights to those assets or their residual cash flows (ring-fenced). The investor controlling the silo consolidates it; others exclude it. Reassess control when facts change in any of the three elements (lapse of rights, termination of a fee contract, change in agent/principal status) — but not merely because market conditions change.
back.explanation: Sub-funds of a mutual fund may be silos.

cards.front: Investment entities: what is the rule?

back.simplified: An investment entity (i) obtains funds from investors to provide investment management services, (ii) commits that its business purpose is to invest solely for capital appreciation and/or investment income, and (iii) measures and evaluates substantially all investments on a fair value basis. Typical characteristics: more than one investment, more than one investor, unrelated investors, equity-type ownership interests. It must have exit strategies ; it must not obtain other benefits from investees. It does not consolidate subsidiaries (measures them at FVTPL), except subsidiaries that are not investment entities and provide investment-related services. Its non-investment-entity parent consoli
back.explanation: Change of status is prospective: ceasing → deemed acquisition at fair value (Ind AS 103); becoming → apply loss-of-control accounting to subsidiaries it stops consolidating. SM Unit 3 Illustrations 21–24; Unit 4 Illustrations 35–36.

cards.front: Goodwill / capital reserve and NCI at the date control is obtained: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Consolidate from the date control is obtained until it is lost. Goodwill = consideration (fair value) + NCI + fair value of previously held interest − net identifiable assets at fair value. A bargain excess goes to OCI → capital reserve where the reason is clear (otherwise directly to capital reserve), attributed to the parent. NCI (present ownership interests) at fair value or proportionate share of net identifiable assets . NCI is presented within equity , separately from owners of the parent.
back.explanation: Income and expenses of the subsidiary are based on acquisition-date fair values — depreciation on the ₹100 lakh fair value, not the ₹80 lakh book value (SM Example 4). Step acquisition: remeasure the earlier stake (see step acquisitions ).
cases: Income and expenses of the subsidiary are based on acquisition-date fair values — depreciation on the ₹100 lakh fair value, not the ₹80 lakh book value (SM Example 4).

cards.front: Step acquisition and control without consideration in consolidation: what is the rule?

back.simplified: On obtaining control in stages, remeasure the previously held interest at acquisition-date fair value; gain or loss to profit or loss (FVOCI amounts are never recycled — they may be transferred within equity to retained earnings on deemed disposal). Without consideration, use the acquisition-date fair value of the acquirer's interest in place of consideration; by contract alone, 100% of the acquiree's net assets may be NCI.
back.explanation: 25% held + 40% bought → control at 65% on 1 April 20X1 (SM Example 1). SM Unit 4 Illustration 5.
cases: 25% held + 40% bought → control at 65% on 1 April 20X1 (SM Example 1).

cards.front: Uniform policies, reporting dates, potential voting rights in allocation: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Use uniform accounting policies for like transactions (adjust a member's statements, e.g. US GAAP to Ind AS). Use the same reporting date; if impracticable, use the subsidiary's most recent statements adjusted for significant transactions, with a difference of no more than three months , consistent from period to period. Allocate profit and equity on existing ownership interests , ignoring potential voting rights — unless they currently give access to the returns, in which case they are reflected and Ind AS 109 does not apply to them.
back.explanation: AS 21 allowed six months and non-uniform policies if impracticable. SM Unit 4 Illustrations 6–9.

cards.front: Intra-group balances, transactions and unrealised profits: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Eliminate intra-group balances, transactions, income and expenses in full . Unrealised profits in inventory, PPE, intangibles and investment property are eliminated in full — even for subsidiaries less than 100% owned; unrealised losses are eliminated unless cost cannot be recovered. Ind AS 12 applies to temporary differences from eliminations.
back.explanation: Upstream (subsidiary → parent) unrealised profit reduces the subsidiary's profit and is shared with NCI; downstream (parent → subsidiary) is borne by the parent (SM Illustrations 14–18). Goods sold on to third parties: only sales and cost of sales are eliminated.
cases: Upstream (subsidiary → parent) unrealised profit reduces the subsidiary's profit and is shared with NCI; downstream (parent → subsidiary) is borne by the parent (SM Illustrations 14–18).
Dividend received from a subsidiary is eliminated against the dividend paid; NCI's share reduces NCI (SM Illustrations 10–13).

cards.front: Memory hook: Intra-group eliminations?

back.simplified: Eliminate 100% always; who bears it depends on who sold (upstream → share with NCI).

back.simplified: Dividend received from a subsidiary is eliminated against the dividend paid; NCI's share reduces NCI (SM Illustrations 10–13).

cards.front: Attributing profit, OCI and losses to NCI: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Attribute profit or loss and each component of OCI to owners of the parent and NCI; total comprehensive income is attributed to NCI even if this results in a deficit balance . If a subsidiary has cumulative preference shares classified as equity and held by NCI, compute the parent's share after deducting those dividends whether or not declared.
back.explanation: SM Example 5: profit ₹5,00,000 − 10% on ₹10,00,000 preference shares ₹1,00,000 = ₹4,00,000 × 80% = ₹3,20,000 to the parent. SM Unit 4 Illustrations 19–20.
cases: SM Example 5: profit ₹5,00,000 − 10% on ₹10,00,000 preference shares ₹1,00,000 = ₹4,00,000 × 80% = ₹3,20,000 to the parent.

cards.front: Changes in ownership without loss of control: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Changes in a parent's ownership interest that do not result in loss of control are equity transactions . Adjust the carrying amounts of controlling and non-controlling interests; recognise directly in equity (attributed to the parent) any difference between the NCI adjustment and the fair value of consideration paid or received. No gain or loss in profit or loss; goodwill is not remeasured ; assets and liabilities are unchanged.
back.explanation: SM Illustration 23: buy 10% of a 70% subsidiary for ₹2,600 thousand; NCI ₹6,600 ÷ 30 × 10 = ₹2,200 thousand; Dr NCI 2,200, Dr other equity 400 / Cr cash 2,600; goodwill unchanged. SM Illustrations 21–27 (sale of 20% of a wholly owned subsidiary, reductions in interest).

cards.front: Memory hook: Buying/selling stakes without losing control?

back.simplified: Still in control? It's an equity deal — no P&L, no goodwill change.

cards.front: Chain holding and sub-subsidiaries: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A sub-subsidiary controlled through a subsidiary is consolidated even if the group's effective interest is below 50%. Effective interest = product of holdings down the chain plus any direct holding; the balance is NCI (direct + indirect). The sub-subsidiary comes under control on the later of the date the parent acquired the subsidiary (if it already held the sub-subsidiary) and the date the subsidiary acquired it — this fixes the pre-acquisition reserves.
back.explanation: P 80% → S1 60% → S2: group 48%, NCI in S1's share 12%, direct NCI 40% (SM Situation 1). P 80% of S1, S1 75% of S2, P 10% direct of S2: group 60% + 10% = 70%, NCI 30% (15% direct + 15% indirect) (Situation 2).

cards.front: Loss of control: what is the rule?

back.simplified: On losing control (sale, partial sale, deemed disposal by dilution): derecognise the subsidiary's assets (including goodwill) and liabilities and the carrying amount of NCI; recognise the fair value of consideration received, any distribution of shares to owners, and any retained interest at fair value (its initial Ind AS 109 fair value or the cost of an associate/JV); reclassify OCI amounts as if the assets/liabilities were disposed of directly (foreign currency reserve to profit or loss; revaluation surplus to retained earnings); recognise the resulting gain or loss in profit or loss attributable to the parent.
back.explanation: Multiple arrangements are treated as one transaction if entered at the same time or in contemplation of each other, form a single transaction, one depends on another, or one is uneconomic alone (SM Illustration 34). Sell 25% then 55% of an 80% stake: the first is an equity transaction, the second triggers P&L — a reason for the single-transaction test (SM Example 9).

back.simplified: Lose control = sell everything at fair value and buy back what you keep at fair value.

cards.front: Joint arrangements and joint control: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A joint arrangement : parties bound by a contractual arrangement that gives two or more of them joint control — contractually agreed sharing of control where decisions about relevant activities require unanimous consent of the parties sharing control. First assess whether all parties or a group collectively control (Ind AS 110), then whether unanimity among them is required. Where a minimum vote can be reached by more than one combination, there is no joint control unless the contract specifies which parties must agree.
back.explanation: Not every party needs joint control: some may merely participate. Unanimity only over protective rights → no joint control (SM Illustration 12). Dispute-resolution clauses do not prevent joint control (Illustration 13).
cases: Unanimity only over protective rights → no joint control (SM Illustration 12). Dispute-resolution clauses do not prevent joint control (Illustration 13).

cards.front: Joint operation vs joint venture: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Joint operation : parties have rights to the assets and obligations for the liabilities . Joint venture : parties have rights to the net assets . Not structured through a separate vehicle → joint operation. Through a separate vehicle → consider (1) the legal form (no separation between parties and vehicle → joint operation); (2) the contractual terms (rights to assets/obligations for liabilities → joint operation); (3) other facts — if the activities primarily provide the parties with output and the parties are substantially the only source of cash flows → joint operation; otherwise joint venture. Guarantees alone do not decide.
back.explanation: Different arrangements under one framework agreement can be of different types (SM Illustration 20). AS 27's jointly controlled operations and assets become joint operations; a jointly controlled entity becomes either type.
cases: Different arrangements under one framework agreement can be of different types (SM Illustration 20).

cards.front: Accounting for joint operations: what is the rule?

back.simplified: A joint operator recognises, in separate and consolidated statements, its assets (incl. share of joint assets), liabilities (incl. share of joint liabilities), revenue from its share of output, its share of revenue from sale of output by the operation, and its expenses (incl. share of joint expenses). Sales/contributions to the operation: gain or loss only to the extent of other parties' interests (losses showing NRV decline or impairment in full). Purchases from it: do not recognise its share of gain/loss until resold (its share of NRV/impairment losses recognised). Acquiring an interest in a joint operation that is a business: apply Ind AS 103 to its share (fair values, acquisition costs e
back.explanation: A party without joint control but with rights to assets and obligations for liabilities accounts like a joint operator; otherwise per the applicable Ind AS. Joint venture: equity method in consolidated statements (Ind AS 28), Ind AS 27 in separate statements; a party without joint control but with significant influence uses Ind AS 28, otherwise Ind AS 109.

sections.title: Associates and the equity method (Ind AS 28)

cards.front: Significant influence: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Significant influence is the power to participate in financial and operating policy decisions, but not control or joint control. Holding 20% or more of voting power (directly or through subsidiaries) presumes significant influence unless clearly demonstrated otherwise; below 20% presumes none unless clearly demonstrated. Evidence: board representation; participation in policy-making (including dividends); material transactions; interchange of managerial personnel; provision of essential technical information. Currently exercisable potential voting rights are considered (ignoring management intention and financial ability). Influence is lost when the power to participate is lost (e.g. investe
back.explanation: A majority held by another investor does not necessarily preclude significant influence. SM Unit 6 Illustrations 1–7.

cards.front: Memory hook: Significant influence (20% presumption)?

back.simplified: 20% presumes influence; Board, Policy, Transactions, People, Technology prove it.

cards.front: The equity method and its procedure: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Initially at cost ; then adjusted for the investor's share of post-acquisition profit or loss (in P&L) and OCI (in OCI); distributions reduce the carrying amount. On acquisition identify goodwill (included in the carrying amount, not amortised) or capital reserve. Adjust the share of profit for depreciation on fair values and impairments. Group share = holdings of the parent and subsidiaries (ignore holdings of other associates/JVs); use the associate's consolidated figures. Upstream and downstream gains/losses recognised only to the extent of unrelated investors' interests (downstream impairment/NRV losses in full; upstream — investor's share). Same reporting date (difference ≤ 3 months); u
back.explanation: Potential voting rights generally ignored in applying the equity method unless they give present access to returns. Non-monetary contribution for equity: as downstream; without commercial substance the gain is unrealised and eliminated against the investment.

cards.front: Memory hook: Equity method procedure?

back.simplified: Cost + share of profit + share of OCI − dividends.

cards.front: Exemptions from the equity method: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Need not apply the equity method if (1) the entity is a parent exempt under Ind AS 110.4(a), or all of: owners informed and not objecting, not publicly traded, not filing, parent publishes Ind AS consolidated statements; (2) the investment is held by or through a venture capital organisation, mutual fund, unit trust or similar (incl. investment-linked insurance funds) — may elect FVTPL per investment at initial recognition; (3) a portion held through such an entity may be measured at FVTPL, with the equity method for the rest.
back.explanation: Mutual fund holding over 20% may measure at FVTPL (SM Example 1). SM Unit 6 Illustration 9.
cases: Mutual fund holding over 20% may measure at FVTPL (SM Example 1). SM Unit 6 Illustration 9.

cards.front: Losses, long-term interests and impairment: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Stop recognising losses when the share of losses equals the interest — the equity-method carrying amount plus long-term interests that are in substance part of the net investment (preference shares, long-term loans whose settlement is not planned; not trade receivables or secured loans). Apply excess losses to those interests in reverse order of seniority ; Ind AS 109 applies to them first. After zero, provide only for legal or constructive obligations or payments made. Resume profits only after they equal unrecognised losses. Test the whole net investment for impairment (Ind AS 36) on objective evidence; impairment is not allocated to goodwill; reversals allowed.
back.explanation: Disappearance of an active market because shares are no longer traded, or a credit downgrade alone, is not evidence of impairment. Value in use: share of the associate's cash flows plus disposal proceeds, or dividends plus disposal proceeds (same result).

cards.front: Discontinuing the equity method; held for sale: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Stop the equity method when the investment ceases to be an associate or JV: becomes a subsidiary → Ind AS 103/110 (remeasure previous interest to fair value, gain/loss in P&L); retained interest is a financial asset → fair value, with P&L gain/loss = (fair value of retained interest + proceeds) − carrying amount; reclassify the investor's share of OCI as if the investee disposed of the items (proportionately on a partial reduction that keeps significant influence). Associate ↔ joint venture : continue the equity method, no remeasurement . A portion classified as held for sale follows Ind AS 105; the rest stays equity-accounted until disposal; if it no longer qualifies, apply the equity metho
back.explanation: Share of foreign currency reserve ₹10,000 reclassified to profit or loss on sale (SM Example 5). SM Unit 6 Illustrations 16–17.
cases: Share of foreign currency reserve ₹10,000 reclassified to profit or loss on sale (SM Example 5).

cards.front: Separate financial statements: what is the rule?

back.simplified: In separate financial statements account for investments in subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures either at cost or in accordance with Ind AS 109 (FVTPL/FVOCI), applying the same accounting for each category. Cost-measured investments held for sale follow Ind AS 105; Ind AS 109-measured ones do not change. Investment entities and entities that elected FVTPL under Ind AS 28 use FVTPL here too. Dividends are recognised in profit or loss when the right to receive is established (generally shareholder approval).
back.explanation: Ind AS 27 applies when an entity elects or is required by law to present separate statements; in India the Companies Act requires every company's own financial statements. Change in investment-entity status: ceasing → cost (fair value as deemed cost) or Ind AS 109; becoming → FVTPL with the difference to profit or loss and FVOCI amounts reclassified (SM Examples 2–3).
cases: Change in investment-entity status: ceasing → cost (fair value as deemed cost) or Ind AS 109; becoming → FVTPL with the difference to profit or loss and FVOCI amounts reclassified (SM Examples 2–3).

cards.front: Disclosure of interests in other entities: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Disclose information to evaluate the nature of, and risks associated with, interests in subsidiaries, joint arrangements, associates and unconsolidated structured entities, and their effects on financial position, performance and cash flows: significant judgements and assumptions (control, joint control, significant influence, type of arrangement); the interest NCI have in the group's activities and cash flows (summarised financial information for subsidiaries with material NCI); restrictions and risks; consequences of changes in ownership without loss of control and of losing control; nature, extent and financial effects of joint arrangements and associates (summarised financial information
back.explanation: Aggregation is allowed for similar entities; not required for post-employment plans or separate-statement interests already disclosed under Ind AS 27.

cards.front: Beyond the SM: deferred tax on consolidation adjustments: what is the rule?

back.simplified: Beyond the study material (Ind AS 12 applied to consolidation). Eliminating unrealised intra-group profit creates a temporary difference between the group carrying amount of the asset and its tax base (which stays with the buyer's tax position); deferred tax is recognised at the buyer's tax rate. The SM's Ind AS 110 vs AS 21 table notes that Ind AS requires deferred taxes on such eliminations while AS 21 did not.
back.explanation: Check the question for a tax rate before computing; ICAI consolidation answers often ignore tax unless asked.

GEM Ltd., an Indian company acquired 75% of the share capital of VEW Ltd. on 30th September, 2020, an entity registered as company in USA. The functional currency of GEM Ltd. is Rupees and its financial year end on 31st March, 2021. The functional currency of VEW Ltd. is USD.
 (i) On 30th September, 2020, the fair value of the Net Assets of VEW Ltd. was USD 10 million and the purchase consideration paid was USD 7.8 million. The exchange rate as at 30th September, 2020 was ₹ 71.5 per USD and at 31st March, 2021 was ₹ 73.5 per USD.
 (ii) VEW Ltd. sold goods costing USD 1.9 million to GEM Ltd. for USD 3.1 million during the year ended 31st March, 2021. The exchange rate on the date of purchase by GEM Ltd. was ₹ 70.5 per USD and on 31st March, 2021 was ₹ 73.5 per USD. 50% of the goods purchased by GEM Ltd. from VEW Ltd. were unsold as at 31st March, 2021.
 For (i) determine the value at which the Goodwill should be recognized in the financial statements of GEM Ltd. as at 31st March, 2021.
 For (ii) determine the unrealized profit to be eliminated in the preparation of consolidated financial statements of GEM Ltd. for the year ending on 31st March, 2021. (6 Marks)

Tiger Gems Ltd. and Mammoth Minerals Ltd. are engaged in extraction of coal and minerals from coal-fields, which they own and operate independently of each other.
 In May 2024, Tiger Gems Ltd. and Mammoth Minerals Ltd. jointly acquired an underground 'Luminuos' Coal mine in the ratio of 55:45. Both the companies agreed to share services and costs. Decisions relating to 'Luminuos' Coal mine requires unanimous agreement of both the parties. No separate entity is incorporated.
 The extraction of coal and minerals from Coal mine is done through huge machines. These machines can extract only upto 95%. The remaining coal is irrecoverable and remains in the Coal mine until the mine is decommissioned. As per the laws in force, the Coal mine should be decommissioned at the end of its useful life.
 (i) Discuss whether the joint arrangement between Tiger Gems Ltd. and Mammoth Minerals Ltd. is a Joint Operation or Joint Venture.
 (ii) Discuss the accounting for the unextracted coal and mineral as per Ind AS 16 and Ind AS 37 with respect to aforesaid 'Luminuous' Coal mine. (5 Marks)
hints: Start from the deciding requirement: Accounting for joint operations.
practice.modelAnswer:
(b) (i) Determination of Joint Arrangement
 As per Ind AS 111 'Joint Arrangements', a joint arrangement is an arrangement of which two or more parties have joint control. Joint control is the contractually agreed sharing of control of an arrangement, which exists only when decisions about the relevant activities require the unanimous consent of the parties sharing control.
 The structure and form of the arrangement determines the nature of the relationship.
 Joint Operation: A joint arrangement which is NOT structured through a separate vehicle is a joint operation. In such a case, the contractual arrangement establishes the parties' rights and obligations.
 Joint Venture: A Joint arrangement whereby the parties that have joint control of the arrangement have rights to the net assets of the arrangement.
 A joint operator accounts for the assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses relating to its involvement in a joint operation in accordance with the relevant Ind AS.
 The arrangement between Tiger Gems Ltd. and Mammoth Minerals Ltd. is a joint operation as no separate vehicle is formed and the companies have agreed to share services and costs with decisions regarding the underground 'Luminous' coal mine requiring unanimous agreement of both the parties.
 Both the companies should recognize their share of the asset as Property, Plant and Equipment.
 (ii) Accounting for the unextracted coal and mineral
 As per para 16 of Ind AS 16 'Property, Plant and Equipment', the cost of an item of property, plant and equipment comprises the initial estimate of the costs of dismantling and removing the item and restoring the site on which it is located.
 Further, para 45 of Ind AS 37 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets', provides that where the effect of the time value of money is material, the amount of a provision shall be the present value of the expenditures expected to be required to settle the obligation.
 Thus, costs incurred by an entity in respect of obligations for dismantling, removing and restoring the site on which an item of property, plant and equipment is situated are recognized and measured in accordance with Ind AS 16 and Ind AS 37.
 Each of the entities in the joint arrangement should recognize their respective share of the cost of decommissioning of the underground storage facility.
 However, as per para 29 of Ind AS 37 where an entity is jointly and severally liable for an obligation, the part of the obligation that is expected to be met by other parties is treated as a contingent liability.
 Accordingly, each of the entities in the joint arrangement should also disclose the share of the cost of decommissioning of the underground facility, to be borne by another joint arrangement entity, as a contingent liability.
 As per Ind AS 16, Property, Plant and Equipment are tangible items that:
 (a) are held for use in the production or supply of goods or services, for rental to others, or for administrative purposes; and
 (b) are expected to be used during more than one period.)
 Thus, both the entities should classify and account for their share of irrecoverable coal and minerals as property, plant and equipment, as the irrecoverable coal and minerals is necessary for the storage facility to perform its function. Therefore, the irrecoverable coal and minerals, being a part of the storage facility, should be capitalized as a component of the storage facility asset, and should be depreciated to its residual value over the life of the storage facility.

Zebra Limited is considering to grant an interest free loan of ₹ 25,00,000 to its wholly owned Indian subsidiary company, Camel Limited. No transaction cost is attached with this loan. With respect to other terms and conditions, the following alternate options are being considered:
 • Option 1: The loan is interest free and is repayable on demand;
 • Option 2: The loan is interest free and is repayable in a single bullet payment after 4 years from the date of granting of such loan. The current market rate of interest for similar loan is 12% per annum.
 • Option 3: The said loan is interest free and will be repaid as and when Camel Limited has funds to repay the loan amount.
 You are required to suggest as per applicable Ind AS, under each of the options, the accounting treatment of the above loan:
 • in the standalone financial statements of Zebra Limited and Camel Limited; and
 • in the consolidated financial statements of Zebra Limited.
 Also give journal entries under option 2.
 Also suggest the accounting treatment as per applicable Ind AS, if in future periods, Camel Limited grants an interest free loan to Zebra Limited. (10 Marks)
hints: Start from the deciding requirement: Separate financial statements.
practice.modelAnswer:
(a) Ind AS 109 requires that a financial assets and liabilities are recognized on initial recognition at its fair value, as adjusted for the transaction cost. In accordance with Ind AS 113, the fair value of a financial liability with a demand feature (e.g., a demand deposit) is not less than the amount payable on demand, discounted from the first date that the amount could be required to be paid.
 Using the guidance, the interest-free loan will be accounted for as below in various scenarios:
 Option 1: Since the loan is repayable on demand, it has fair value equal to cash consideration given i.e. ₹ 25,00,000. The parent and subsidiary recognize financial asset and liability, respectively, at the amount of loan given. Going forward, no interest is accrued on the loan. Upon repayment, both the parent and the subsidiary reverse the entries made at origination.
 Option 2: The loan is repayable in single bullet payment after 4 years. Both parent and subsidiary recognize financial asset and liability, respectively, at fair value on initial recognition. The difference between the loan amount and its fair value is treated as an equity contribution to the subsidiary. This represents a further investment by the parent in the subsidiary.
